subject: PMP
body: Two team members disagree strongly about a technical approach. What should the project manager do first?
options: Ignore it until it affects the schedule
Choose the approach personally and move on
Meet with both to understand each view and find a collaborative solution
explanation: Collaborating/problem solving is usually best for lasting resolution.

subject: PMP
body: A new hybrid team is struggling to work together. Which action best supports team performance?
options: Agree a team charter with ground rules and working agreements
Hold all meetings in person only
explanation: A team charter sets shared values and working norms.

subject: PMP
body: In an agile team, who is primarily responsible for removing impediments?
options: The servant leader (e.g. Scrum Master / project manager)

subject: PMP
body: A team member is consistently missing deadlines. What should the project manager do first?
options: Raise it in the next team meeting
Talk with the team member privately to understand the cause
explanation: Address issues privately and seek root causes.

subject: PMP
body: A stakeholder requests a significant change during execution. What should the project manager do first?
options: Evaluate the impact of the change
Ask the team to work overtime
Implement it to keep the stakeholder happy
explanation: Then submit it through integrated change control.

subject: PMP
body: Which document formally authorises a project and the project manager?

subject: PMP
body: A risk has occurred. What should the project manager do?
options: Add it to the lessons learned only
Ignore it if it is small
Implement the planned risk response and update the issue log
explanation: Once a risk occurs it becomes an issue.

subject: PMP
body: What is the main purpose of a retrospective?
options: To inspect how the team works and agree improvements
To demo the product to stakeholders

subject: PMP
body: Which estimating technique uses the weighted average (O + 4M + P) / 6?

subject: PMP
body: A project has CPI 0.8 and SPI 1.1. What does this mean?
options: Over budget and ahead of schedule

subject: PMP
body: When should lessons learned be captured?

subject: PMP
body: A new regulation will affect the project. What should the project manager do first?
options: Assess the impact on the project
explanation: Then update plans through change control.

subject: PMP
body: What is the main purpose of a benefits management plan?
options: To describe how and when the project's benefits will be delivered and measured
explanation: Links the project to business value.

subject: PMP
body: Which approach best suits a project with highly uncertain, changing requirements?
options: A fixed-price contract with frozen scope
